pdf_preview_contract.open: read_pdf emits exactly one pdf_open metadata event with opaque preview_id and total_bytes, then retains a descriptor lease until cancellation, connection loss or idle timeout. Structural parsing and passwords belong to PDF.js, not the indexing parser.
pdf_preview_contract.range: read_pdf_range accepts exactly preview_id, begin, end (exclusive); at most 65536 bytes per request, validated against one observed source identity before and after IO. Returns exactly preview_id, offset, bytes. No total document byte limit.
pdf_preview_contract.ownership: At most four native preview leases. Cancel the owning read_pdf request to close. All ordinary protocol frame, queue and active request bounds apply. No paths or native identity fields leave the backend.
pdf_preview_contract.request_ids: The reserved pdf:<canonical positive u128 decimal> namespace is exclusively for read_pdf_range. Its strictly increasing high-water mark rejects replay without retained history or general session-request accounting. All other request IDs retain the unchanged no-reuse/4096-request policy. No range is replayed after backend restart.

error.message: This capability is not implemented in the foundation build.
Request IDs must not be reused within a connection.

cancellation_contract.accepted: Before final commit, cancellation atomically wins, prevents begin_commit, and produces exactly one cancelled terminal followed by cancel_ack accepted:true.
cancellation_contract.rejected: cancel_ack accepted:false means unknown/completed ID OR an active request already sealed for final commit. It is not terminal; an active caller must await its actual result/error, not reject on the local cancel signal.
cancellation_contract.final_commit: Cancellation::begin_commit returns a one-way CommitPermit. Dropping it never unseals cancellation, including COMMIT failure or panic. Protection lasts through queued terminal publication; success/error remains authoritative. Sealed handlers returning Cancelled are reported as internal error, not rollback.
cancellation_contract.shutdown: EOF/input shutdown cancels pre-commit work and drains sealed work. Output failure/stall stops publication but still drains sealed work before serve returns a transport error. No commit timeout is imposed; handlers must join bounded native finalization. Forced termination or lost output means unknown outcome, never proof of success/rollback; do not automatically replay mutations.
cancellation_contract.partial_progress: This seal is for final-request commit/publication, NOT each intermediate indexing transaction. Durable partial-progress and later cancellation semantics must be defined by indexing integration.
